questions.prompt: Match each page to the render mode that suits it best.

pairs.left: A blog post that is the same for everyone
A product page with live prices

questions.explanation: Prerender what is identical for everyone, server-render public dynamic pages, and client-render private pages.

options.text: Downloading data before the app starts
The browser-side app reusing the server-rendered DOM instead of rebuilding it
Compressing the HTML on the server
Rendering pages at build time

questions.explanation: With provideClientHydration(), Angular adopts the existing DOM and attaches listeners, avoiding a flash and extra work.

questions.prompt: Where should code that reads localStorage go in an SSR app?

options.text: In a field initializer
In ngOnInit
In afterNextRender(), which runs only in the browser
In the constructor, before anything else

questions.explanation: Constructors, field initializers, and ngOnInit also run on the server, where localStorage does not exist.

questions.prompt: How does Angular avoid calling the same API on the server and again in the browser?

options.text: It does not; every request runs twice
The HTTP transfer cache embeds GET/HEAD responses in the HTML for HttpClient to reuse
The browser blocks the second request
Prerendering removes all HTTP requests

questions.explanation: provideClientHydration() enables the transfer cache. Requests with an Authorization header are not cached by default.

questions.prompt: With incremental hydration enabled, what does @defer (hydrate on viewport) { <app-reviews /> } do?

options.text: Skips server rendering of the reviews entirely
Renders the reviews on the server and loads/hydrates their JavaScript when they scroll into view
Hydrates the reviews immediately
Prerenders the reviews at build time

questions.explanation: The HTML is shown immediately; hydration (downloading and running the code) waits for the trigger.

options.text: Using @if and @for in templates
Setting element.innerHTML directly in ngOnInit
Binding [class.active]="isActive()"
Using signals for component state

questions.explanation: Changing the DOM behind Angular's back makes the browser DOM differ from the server's, which causes hydration mismatch errors.
